report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of graph_delta.py: mutation loop, CLI, specificity arm, per-function refs and deltas; verified claims, found a broken docstring claim and a silent parsing risk.
risks: graph_delta.py:561-575 | medium | The comment 'An unparsable half is not a detection and not a failure of the detector; counting it either way would move the headline for a bookkeeping reason' claims a skip is neutral, but the mutation is still counted in row['n'], so an unparsable half actually does move the headline: it lowers the detected rate without being a true negative. | Check whether the comment intends 'n' to exclude unparsable mutations; if so, the counting logic is wrong.

graph_delta.py:660-664 | medium | _git silently returns None on any non-zero exit (including git not found or permission errors), and callers treat None as 'no output' (e.g., 'no python files'), so a failure is indistinguishable from an empty result. | Verify whether a non-zero exit can occur for reasons other than 'no commits/files'; if so, the function should distinguish error from empty.

graph_delta.py:700-701 | low | measure_commit silently skips files where either before or after fails to parse (continue), and the skip is not recorded in rec['skipped'] or any counter, so the report undercounts files and could mislead the specificity distribution. | Check whether parse failures are expected to be rare; if not, they should be counted or reported.

handoff.purpose: Mutation analysis loop, CLI entry, specificity arm with real commits, per-function reference deltas.

symbols.name: _int_arg
symbols.note: Parses an integer from argv after a flag; silently returns default on ValueError/IndexError.

symbols.name: _git
symbols.note: Runs a git command in the repo root, returns None on non-zero exit, else stdout (bytes or decoded string).

symbols.name: commit_shas
symbols.note: Returns non-merge commit SHAs touching Python files, newest first, limited to limit.

symbols.name: measure_commit
symbols.note: Computes per-file added/removed refs and type edges for a single commit; returns a record with totals and per-file details.

symbols.name: specificity
symbols.note: Runs measure_commit over a set of real commits and aggregates specificity statistics (moved, pure deletions).

symbols.name: _refs_by_function
symbols.note: Parses Python source and returns a dict mapping function names to Counter of reference names/attributes, excluding docstrings.

symbols.name: function_deltas
symbols.note: Returns one row per function present in both before and after, with added and removed reference counts.

claims.text: An unparsable half is not a detection and not a failure of the detector; counting it either way would move the headline for a bookkeeping reason.
claims.why: The mutation is still counted in row['n'] (line 574), so an unparsable half does move the headline: it lowers the detected rate without being a true negative. The claim that it is 'not counted either way' is contradicted by the code.

claims.text: ``--limit 40``, or the default. Silent fallback is deliberate: a malformed limit should not lose the run, and the value is echoed in the written report either way.
claims.why: The function catches ValueError/IndexError and returns default; the value is used in the report (e.g., 'limit' in specificity output).

claims.text: Non-merge commits touching Python, newest first. Merges are excluded because a merge's diff against its first parent attributes other people's work to it, which would pollute the corpus with changes it did not make.
claims.why: The git command uses '--no-merges' and '--format=%H' with paths '*.py'; the output is split into lines preserving order (newest first by git default).

claims.text: A sweeping commit would dominate the distribution for a reason that has nothing to do with defectiveness. Bounded and SAID, never silently cut.
claims.why: The code checks len(files) > max_files and sets rec['skipped'] with the reason, returning early; it is not silently cut.

claims.text: The same layer delta, for one real commit. Returns per-file and totals.
claims.why: The function returns a dict with totals and per_file list; it uses _ast_refs and _type_edge_keys to compute deltas.

claims.text: This repository's history is nearly all growth (median +354 references per commit, median -0), so any 'removed vs added' rule is trivially never true at commit scale, and a guard deleted beside a new 300-line module is invisible.
claims.why: The claimed medians are external data not present in this chunk; the reasoning about scale is a rationale, not a checkable behavior.

claims.text: A seeded defect edits ONE function; so the comparison has to be one function wide or the signal drowns in the rest of the patch.
claims.why: This is a design rationale; the code does implement per-function granularity, but the claim about seeded defects is external.

claims.text: Qualify by line so two same-named methods in one file stay distinct.
claims.why: The code does not qualify by line; it uses only node.name as the key (line 713). Two methods with the same name in one file are merged into one counter.

claims.text: Functions added or removed wholesale are excluded: a new function has no 'before' to lose references against, and counting it as a huge addition would swamp the distribution the rule is read from.
claims.why: The code iterates only over set(fb) & set(fa), so functions present in only one version are excluded.

claims.text: The mutation corpus contains only BAD patches, so it measures sensitivity and cannot measure specificity at all.
claims.why: The claim about the mutation corpus contents is not verifiable from this chunk; the specificity arm is implemented in code, but the corpus description is external.

claims.text: This arm runs REAL COMMITS through the identical pipeline so the two distributions can be compared.
claims.why: The specificity arm uses the same layer delta functions (_ast_refs, _type_edge_keys) as the mutation loop, running on real commit SHAs.

claims.text: The hypothesis is stated before the run, from the shape of the first result: five of the seven detected mutations were PURE DELETIONS (``+0/-N``).
claims.why: The specific first result data is not present in this chunk; only the hypothesis is stated.

claims.text: Seeded defects disable things — they remove a guard, a call, a check — while real work usually adds or exchanges.
claims.why: This is a general claim about seeded defects and real work, not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: So the candidate discriminator is not 'did the delta move' but 'did it move in the DELETING direction only'.
claims.why: The code computes pure_deletion as added == 0 and removed > 0, which is exactly the 'deleting direction only' discriminator.

observations.what: The mutation loop's comment claims unparsable halves are not counted either way, but the mutation is still counted in row['n'].
_refs_by_function comment says 'Qualify by line' but the key is only the function name, so same-named methods merge.
_git returns None on any non-zero exit, and callers treat None as empty output, so failures are silently reported as 'no data'.
measure_commit skips unparseable files silently without recording the skip in rec['skipped'].
